analysis.investment_thesis: Aadhar Housing Finance is a pure-play affordable housing lender riding India's most powerful structural tailwind — housing for the bottom-of-pyramid segment — with a 33.4% net profit CAGR over six years at a still-reasonable 20.8x P/E. The PEG ratio is well below 1, making this one of the better risk-reward propositions in the NBFC/HFC universe today.
key_strengths: Exceptional net profit CAGR of 33.4% (FY19→FY25: INR 162 Cr to INR 912 Cr), far outpacing revenue growth — NIM expansion at work
Structural tailwind from India's affordable housing deficit, PMAY government push, and low mortgage penetration in sub-INR 15 lakh ticket size segment
P/E of 20.8x is reasonable for this quality of growth; forward P/E of 16.2x implies further earnings re-rating potential
key_risks: Promoter is Blackstone (PE firm, 64.9%) — eventual exit overhang and potential block deals could pressure share price
D/E of 2.55x is high even by HFC standards; any tightening of wholesale funding markets or ALM mismatch could stress the book
ROE of 16.9% is decent but not exceptional for the leverage employed — needs to cross 20%+ as capital base builds
red_flags: PE promoter means this is not a founder-led business with decades-long alignment — Blackstone will exit at some point
Negative OCF every single year (inherent to HFCs, but cumulative cash consumption of INR 9,847 Cr over 5 years requires constant capital markets access)
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aadhar Housing Finance operates in the most underpenetrated segment of India's mortgage market — ticket sizes below INR 15 lakh to first-time home buyers in tier 2-4 towns. Revenue grew 16.1% CAGR since FY19, but the real story is profitability: net profit compounded at 33.4%, going from INR 162 Cr to INR 912 Cr, while finance costs grew at only 8.2% CAGR, demonstrating powerful NIM leverage. EBITDA CAGR of 21.1% over 3 years confirms the operating momentum is real and not a base-effect illusion.

The balance sheet has scaled from INR 12,366 Cr to INR 25,083 Cr in assets over 5 years, with equity base more than doubling to INR 6,894 Cr in FY25 (likely supported by IPO proceeds). D/E at 2.55x is elevated but standard for HFCs. The negative OCF every year is not a red flag in isolation — for a lending business, loan disbursements flow through OCF. The real watch item is credit quality and asset quality, which cannot be fully assessed from the data provided. At current valuations, this is a solid compounding candidate for 5+ years.
